summary.headline: July cooled to seasonal norms: $678K closed won, HIH fell to 26, and June's inflated MQL/SQL numbers washed out of the base.
summary.body: July closed $677,915 across 30 deals (56% win rate by count, 80% by dollar) — down from June's import-and-buying-peak-inflated $970K, but right on pace for the Jul-Aug seasonal lull. HIH fell to 26 (from 76) and the product-tagged funnel (IJ, Inkwell, WH) softened 25-33%, tracking the summer off-season rather than signaling a demand problem. MQL-to-SQL conversion normalized to a healthy 70.9% once June's one-time offline import washed out of the comparison. Watch items: UTM completeness is still just 7.7% of new contacts, and Enterprise segment win rate slipped to 50% on two mid-size losses.

brand_lift.note: These are Google Search numbers, not social engagement — how often our brand and channels surface when people search. YouTube and Instagram were verified as GSC Social Signals properties on Jul 30, 2026; collection starts at verification (no backfill). First WoW read: week of Aug 17. First clean MoM: early-October digest (September vs August). LinkedIn has no GSC connector — it's owned by Microsoft and isn't integrated with Google.

current.narrative: The week of Aug 3 brought a strong back-to-school inbound wave: 60 MQLs came in — up 82% from 33 last week — and High Intent Handraisers [HIH] tripled to 10, the highest since early July. IJ led lower-funnel momentum with 14 MQLs and 9 SQLs, while GF8 (TK/Pre-K) surfaced meaningfully for the first time this season with 22 MQLs — a signal worth tracking as early TK adopters gear up. SQL and Opp held at 30 each with healthy conversion, Single/Small inbound accounting for 60% of new high-intent leads. Open pipeline at 29 district and 23 school deals as several SY26-27 renewals closed won this week ($413K MTD).

previous.narrative: MQL came in at 33 this week (Jul 27–Aug 2), down 17% from 40 the prior week, consistent with the seasonal transition into August. SQL and Opp followed at 23 and 22 — all three metrics in the typical summer-floor range with no structural signal behind the pullback. IJ continues to drive most lower-funnel movement (6 of 23 SQLs), while Single/Small inbound accounts for the majority of new MQLs. Open pipeline holds at 30 district and 24 school deals heading into back-to-school season.
